subject: Prediction over large grids with INLA

messages.author: 334c7505e0b5cf65
messages.subject: Prediction over large grids with INLA
parts:
Hi,

I have a model (covariates + SPDE) that I need to use to predict over a grid with more than 27K points. The model takes about 15 minutes to run using the observed data alone and INLA crashes when I try to use the full grid for prediction. I am considering splitting the grid into smaller blocks and then fit each model separately, but I am not sure whether this will make all the predictions to be based on EXACTLY the same fitted model. I suspect that if I fit the same model with the same data and a different block for prediction then INLA can fit slightly different models. Is this correct? Then, what will be the best way to do this prediction in parallel?

Many thanks,

Virgilio

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Prediction over large grids with INLA
parts:
My recommendation for large scale prediction is to either
1) predict onto the mesh points only, and interpolate the means and standard deviations to the grid afterwards, or
2) use posterior samples to evaluate on the grid

Method 2) is available in the predict() function if you use inlabru. With raw inla, you’ll have to deal with inla.stack for the inla call and inla.posterior.sample for the samples.

Method 1) in raw inla still requires inla.stack, but the postprocessing is a simple inla.mesh.project call.

Finn
